verdicts.verify_by: txtar tests/judge-22-run-realm-address.txtar: gnoland start, the same gnokey maketx run script twice from test1; the script crosses into gno.land/r/demo/xr, prints reflect.Of of its own package var and local, then hands a new(int) to xr.Keep and prints reflect.Of of it
verdicts.tldr: no maketx run object ever reports an address from the run realm's clock: the script's own objects stay ok=false, and an object a realm keeps is stamped by that realm's persisted clock
verdicts.details: Vm Run calls m.RunMemPackage(memPkg, false) (keeper.go:1623), so the run package is never made real and its realm finalize stamps nothing: reflect.Of on the script's package var and on a local returns ok=false after a crossing call returns. A run package cannot declare a crossing function of its own ('crossing function (realm first argument) declared in non-realm package'), so no frame of the script finalizes its own realm mid-transaction. An object the script hands to a realm is adopted by assignNewObjectID (realm.go:2004-2010) and takes that realm's counter, which persists: run 1 reports xr id :8, run 2 reports :10, two addresses.
verdicts.evidence: go test ./gno.land/pkg/integration/ -run 'TestTestdata/judge-22-run-realm-address$' -count=1 -p 1 -parallel 1 -v at 58b269206: PASS; run 1 'pkgvar-after-ping ok: false', 'local-after-ping ok: false', 'kept ok: true ... id: 0081c10c...:8 addr: g142tvvyw72lsnqyye0rgf3jktprucr6fm7t8dd6'; run 2 'kept ok: true ... id: 0081c10c...:10 addr: g1l8xp32fghjfxwv2y0jwkyvtpy8eje7aengaee5'
